read_this_first: Run 4. Same pages, same browser, same search for the first success, same success rule (the page's full reward) and the same scored instances as V3. ONLY THE LEARNER DIFFERS. Checked: on every one of the 130 tasks the stage, the first success found and what finding it cost are identical to V3, and so is every per-instance outcome of the three arms the learner has no part in (random, verbatim, existing_compiler). THE NUMBERS TO QUOTE ARE THE ONES ON INSTANCES NOBODY HAD LOOKED AT (fresh_instances; seeds 1020-1039; the V3 skills were scored there too): tasks at or above 90 percent of 130, from one success 26 -> 34, with three practice instances 30 -> 38; successes of 1380, 792 -> 939 and 908 -> 1021. On the instances scored in the runs (seeds 1000-1019, the summary below) the same counts are 29 -> 39 and 34 -> 44 (where replaying the demonstration is not enough: 19 -> 29 and 24 -> 34; denied the instruction 0 -> 0), AND THOSE ARE TOO HIGH: the producer wrote the four additions below after reading, task by task and instance by instance, where the V3 skills stopped on exactly those instances. Over all 40 instances per task the counts are 26 -> 34 and 30 -> 38. No task is held out in any of this. WHAT THE LEARNER GAINED, all of it read off recorded successes: (1) a run of presses that went through exactly the elements of one kind the instruction mentions is one step, 'press every one of them', and serves pages that name none, one or twelve; (2) a press after which the next target first appeared is remembered as made to bring it out, and on a page where the target is not there, elements of the same kind are pressed, each at most once and at most 12, until it is; (3) an element's text may start or end with a piece the instruction quotes; (4) typed text may be copied from an element that is itself found through the instruction. On the fresh instances, newly at or above 90 percent with practice: click-checkboxes, click-checkboxes-large, click-checkboxes-transfer, click-collapsible-2, click-collapsible-2-nodelay, click-tab-2, click-tab-2-hard, read-table; fallen below: none; fewer successes than the V3 skill: use-autocomplete 17 -> 13, use-autocomplete-nodelay 17 -> 13 with practice, none from one success. WHAT THE FRESH INSTANCES FOUND. At or above 90 percent on the scored instances and not on the fresh ones, with practice: click-button-sequence, click-test-2, click-test-transfer, email-inbox-noscroll, use-autocomplete, use-autocomplete-nodelay. Three causes. (a) AN INSTRUMENT FAULT, in every run so far: a press lands on the centre of the element's box, and where another element covers that point the other element is pressed. A person presses the part that shows. click-test-2 puts two buttons at random places that sometimes overlap; the skill picks the right button and the press hits the one on top (seen directly on seeds 1023 and 1027). click-test-transfer and click-button-sequence fail on the same instances (19 of 20 on the scored instances, 16 of 20 on the fresh ones, all three). Not fixed in this run. (b) use-autocomplete and its no-delay twin ask in two ways ('starts with X and ends with Y' / 'starts with X'). The three practice instances show only the first. Addition (3) makes the first program good enough to pass practice by itself, so no second way is learned, and on the second way it stops after typing (seen on seeds 1021, 1025, 1026); the V3 skill failed in practice and was sent to find another route, which serves both. From one success the V4 skill is far better there, with practice it is worse. (c) email-inbox-noscroll, 20 of 20 on the scored instances against 15 of 20 on the fresh ones with the same skill; the cause was not looked into. THE PRICE OF (2): of the 3510 actions the practice arm took while being scored in the run, 175 were presses made only to look, in 5 tasks (presses_made_only_to_look); they are made inside the one try an instance gets. WHAT WAS NOT DONE. The question 'does the order of the presses matter' was never put to a real page (pages_asked_whether_the_order_of_presses_matters is empty: the search already presses in the order of the page), so that part is tested on written pages only. The one-memory measurement (one agent holding every skill, never told the task) was repeated with these skills on the scored instances only, not on fresh ones (one_memory below). The learner got slower: 6697 seconds summed over tasks against 4905. Checked by the producer only; nobody else has run this.
